sources.page_context: t $50 billion to businesses Ben Werschkul · Washington Correspondent July 13, 2026 2 min read The US sent out $49.1 billion in tariff refunds in June as the checks to businesses accelerated in the second full month of payouts after the US Supreme Court invalidated President Trump's blanket tariffs. That figure handily beat the $23.6 billion in tariff revenue collected over the same period, according to the US Treasury Department's monthly statement . Monday's newly released figures marked a sharp escalation from May's results , which saw the tariff refund process get underway in earnest but with similar refund and revenue figures of around $21.9 billion seen on both sides of the ledger. Tariff Refunds Raise Deficit Concerns The $49.2 billion rebates paid in June helped push the Treasury into the red last month, with the federal budget deficit reaching $120 billion compared with a surplus of $27 billion a year prior. However, the Treasury collected $23.6 billion in customs duties in June, meaning the refunds resulted in a net outflow of $25.6 billion. The figures have nevertheless raised concerns among fiscal hawks, with Maya MacGuineas, president of the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget (CRFB) calling the monthly statement "alarming."
